title: Rohit Sharma: How India's Captain Led His Country to the T20 World Cup
summary: Rohit Sharma's captaincy of India has been defined by calm authority, tactical intelligence, and an ability to get the best from an extraordinary generation of players. The 2024 T20 World Cup triumph was the crowning achievement of his leadership.
content:
Cricket captaincy is one of sport's most complex challenges. You are responsible for eleven individuals, each with their own needs, insecurities, and ideas about the game. You must make tactical decisions under pressure, manage relationships with selectors and administrators, and somehow maintain your own form as a player while carrying the weight of an entire nation's expectations.

Rohit Sharma has done all of this — and in June 2024, led India to the T20 World Cup title that the country had been chasing since their 2007 triumph under MS Dhoni. The victory, coming after years of near-misses in knockout tournaments, was both a sporting achievement and a vindication of a leadership style that had occasionally been questioned.

The Captaincy Record

Rohit took over the full-time Test captaincy from Virat Kohli in 2022 and the T20 captaincy had effectively been his since 2017, when India began to show just how well a team could perform under his direction in the shorter formats.

His IPL record as Mumbai Indians captain was already extraordinary — five titles, the most by any captain in the tournament's history. But leading Mumbai Indians is a different challenge from leading India, where the scrutiny is greater, the opposition stronger, and the margin for error smaller.

His Style of Leadership

Rohit leads with a calmness that the game's most stressful moments rarely disturb. Where Kohli's captaincy was characterised by visible intensity — passion expressed outwardly, celebrated and criticised in equal measure — Rohit's approach is quieter, more measured. He backs his players publicly and absolutely. He does not panic when plans go wrong. And he has an ability to read the game tactically that has consistently impressed those who analyse cricket closely.

His management of India's bowling attack has been particularly noted. Knowing when to take pace off the ball, when to bring on a spinner, when to use a death-overs specialist — these decisions accumulate across a tournament and can decide whether a team wins or loses at the knockout stage.

When you captain India, you learn to manage pressure differently. The expectations are enormous. What I have learned is that the best thing I can do for my team is to be calm myself — because if the captain is calm, the players can be calm, and calm players make better decisions.

The 2024 World Cup

India went into the 2024 T20 World Cup, co-hosted by the USA and West Indies, as favourites. But favourites in knockout cricket often find ways to lose — the pressure accumulates, the margins close, and a team that has dominated for months can fall apart in a single match.

India did not fall apart. They navigated the Super 8s without defeat, produced a stunning semi-final performance against England, and in the final against South Africa, held their nerve when the match hung in the balance. India won by seven runs in a finish that left millions of viewers breathless.

Rohit, in the post-match press conference, did not take credit. He spoke about his players, about the support staff, about the fans. That, too, is part of what good captaincy looks like.

What His Legacy Will Be

Rohit Sharma is one of the greatest opening batters the game has seen — his record of six double centuries in Test cricket, his ODI exploits, his T20 hitting are all extraordinary. But his legacy may ultimately be defined by what he achieved as captain: a T20 World Cup, a generation of players who flourished under his leadership, and a team that learned to win when it mattered most.
